verification_log.DIRECT_FETCH_CONTRADICTS_SEARCH_CONSENSU: A direct fetch of https://help.netflix.com/en/node/24926 returned the SAME four-tier US table this file already has (Mobile $2.99, Basic $3.99, Standard $7.99, Premium $9.99), describing it as current. That table is almost certainly stale or wrong on its face: the US market has never had a 'Mobile' tier (that is an India-specific tier) and Netflix discontinued 'Basic' in the US in 2024/2025 per multiple independent, mutually-consistent web searches reporting the current US structure as Standard-with-Ads $8.99 / Standard $19.99 / Premium $26.99. I am NOT confident enough to pick one answer: the help-center fetch is nominally a primary source but internally implausible; the search results are secondary/aggregator but internally consistent and consistent with well-established facts. This is a genuine, unresolved conflict between two verification methods, not a confidence gap I can close with another search query.

verification_log.decision: SUPERSEDED — this was WRONG. Adopted the US-market web-search-consensus structure ($8.99/$19.99/$26.99, Basic discontinued) for a Bangladesh-scoped facts file. The error: Netflix runs country-specific tier structures, not one global structure, and multiple independent sources describing the US market's 2024-2025 price increase do not establish what Bangladesh is billed. Country-scoping was not kept distinct from market-wide reporting. Corrected below.

verification_log.method: direct fetch of https://www.netflix.com/bd/ (the actual Bangladesh-scoped official URL, not a help-center article or aggregator) plus two further Bangladesh-scoped web searches
verification_log.decision: RESTORED the original four-tier Mobile $2.99 / Basic $3.99 / Standard $7.99 / Premium $9.99 structure (480p/720p/1080p/4K+HDR, 1/1/2/4 simultaneous streams respectively). The direct fetch of netflix.com/bd itself states 'Starts at USD 2.99... Plans range from USD 2.99 to USD 9.99/month' — a primary source, correctly scoped to Bangladesh, confirming this range. Multiple independent searches scoped to Bangladesh specifically (not the US) consistently name all four tiers and prices. Netflix charges Bangladesh accounts in USD (no local BDT price list) and uses a lower-tier structure retained in Bangladesh/South-Asia-class markets, distinct from the higher 3-tier US structure reported in the prior (incorrect) pass. verified_on bumped on this corrected, properly country-scoped basis.
verification_log.lesson: Provider pricing must be scoped by country, currency and effective date before being treated as a reference — the same provider can legitimately show different structures in different markets at the same time. Do not substitute one market's reporting for another's without an explicit same-country source.

netflix.billing_note: Netflix does not bill Bangladesh in BDT; accounts are charged in USD, so the exact BDT amount depends on card/bank FX conversion at the time of billing.

youtube.price_policy: Use live YouTube checkout as authority; verified official help confirms Bangladesh availability and household rules but this cohort does not publish an unverified exact BDT checkout price.
